docs.title: About NDAC
docs.text:
The Nutrien Digital Agriculture Centre (NDAC) at the University of Saskatchewan develops data-driven tools for precision agriculture and environmental monitoring across the Canadian prairies.

All data is managed under:

  • Tri-Agency Research Data Management Policy
  • OCAP® Principles (Ownership · Control · Access · Possession)
  • CARE Principles for Indigenous data governance
  • CRDCN standards

docs.title: Contact
docs.text: Thuan Ha — Data Manager, NDAC Thuan.ha@usask.ca Nutrien Digital Agriculture Centre, University of Saskatchewan

docs.title: How the process works
docs.text:
NDAC operates a discovery-first data portal. You explore dataset descriptions here, then contact us if a dataset is relevant to your research or collaboration.

Discover → Review → Inquire → NDAC Triage → Response → (Approval + Conditions)

docs.title: Step-by-step
docs.text:
1. Discover a dataset Browse the dataset catalog and read the dataset page that interests you.

2. Review the documentation Each dataset page includes a summary, resolution, temporal coverage, data types, and access level.

3. Send an inquiry Email Thuan.ha@usask.ca with:

What to include Why Dataset ID (e.g. NDAC-CROPMASK-PRAIRIES-F25T25) Identifies the exact dataset Your name and organisation Establishes who is requesting Purpose of the request Helps NDAC assess fit Intended use Required for restricted datasets Preferred timeline Helps prioritise responses Whether collaboration is of interest Opens additional paths

4. NDAC reviews your request We will assess: dataset shareability, sensitivity, partner constraints, and whether a meeting is needed first.

5. We respond Possible outcomes:

  • Share general information only
  • Request clarification or schedule a call
  • Approve access in principle (with conditions)
  • Defer due to restrictions or partner agreements

6. If approved — conditions are documented Approved access includes: permitted files, permitted uses, attribution expectations, and any data-sharing agreement requirements.

docs.title: Access levels explained
docs.text:
Badge Meaning Open Publicly available or openly licensed; source links provided where applicable Internal Available to NDAC team members; external access requires discussion Restricted Formal request required; sensitivity or partner constraints apply By Request Contact the NDAC data team to discuss access

Response time

We aim to respond to all inquiries within 5 business days. Complex requests involving restricted or partner data may take longer.

Contact us →

docs.title: NDAC Data Team
docs.text: Thuan Ha — Data Manager Nutrien Digital Agriculture Centre (NDAC) University of Saskatchewan 📧 Thuan.ha@usask.ca

docs.title: What to include in your message
docs.text:
To help us respond efficiently, please include:

  • The dataset ID you are interested in
  • Your name, role, and organisation
  • A brief description of your research purpose or intended use
  • Whether you are seeking a collaboration or a one-time data request

docs.title: 🌤️ The High Resolution Deterministic Precipitation Analysis (HRDPA) Daily Precipitation
docs.text: Processed Internal

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Daily HRDPA precipitation data at approximately 2.5 km resolution are collected for the April–November growing-season period and clipped to the Canadian Prairies region. Missing HRDPA dates are gap-filled using ERA5-Land daily precipitation to create a spatially and temporally complete dataset for agricultural and environmental analyses.

docs.title: 📍 Soil pedon
docs.text: Processed Restricted

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The National Pedon Database (NPDB), produced by Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, contains quality-assessed and standardized soil-profile observations collected across Canada. It includes location information and measurements for more than 100 soil properties, with historical records dating to 1943. The published dataset represents a vetted subset of the complete NPDB holdings and supports digital soil mapping, soil assessment, and environmental modelling. Data are available in CSV, XLSX, GeoJSON, and File Geodatabase formats under the Open Government Licence – Canada. Source: Government of Canada

Field Details Dataset ID CANSOIL-PEDON-POINT-F26T26 Category Field Surveys Project PPSN Owner ACI Primary Contact Thuan Ha Data types Vector Formats csv Status Processed Last updated 2026-04-08

docs.title: 🗺️ Prairie Cropland Mask
docs.text: Processed Internal

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This dataset provides annual 10 m cropland masks for the Canadian Prairies - Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba - from 2017 to 2024. It was developed using 64-band Google AlphaEarth satellite embeddings and a Random Forest classifier trained with Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada’s Annual Crop Inventory. The annual classifications were combined into a cropland-frequency layer, and pixels identified as cropland in more than two years were used to create a stable persistent-cropland mask. The GeoTIFF dataset supports agricultural monitoring, land-use assessment, yield modelling, soil and climate studies, and geospatial machine-learning applications

Field Details Dataset ID NDAC-CROPMASK-PRAIRIES-F25T25 Category Thematic Map Products Owner ACI Primary Contact Thuan Ha Spatial resolution 10 m Temporal coverage 2024 Data types Raster Formats tiff Status Processed Last updated 2025-06-21

docs.title: 🗺️ Prairie Cropland Type
docs.text: Raw Open

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The AAFC Annual Crop Inventory (ACI) provides annual crop-type and land-cover maps for the Canadian Prairies from 2009 to 2025. Produced by Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada using satellite imagery and ground-reference data, it is a categorical raster dataset with a spatial resolution of 56 m for 2009–2010 and 30 m from 2011 onward. The inventory has a target overall accuracy of at least 85% and is available under the Open Government Licence – Canada 2.0.

Field Details Dataset ID NDAC-CROPTYPE-PRAIRIES-F09T25 Category Thematic Map Products Owner AAFC Spatial resolution 30 m Temporal coverage 2009 - 2025 Data types Raster Formats tiff Status Raw Last updated 2025-09-02

docs.title: ⛰️ Digital Elevation Model (DEM) - TanDemX
docs.text: Raw Internal

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The TanDEM-X Digital Elevation Model, obtained through the DLR EOWEB portal, provides elevation data at approximately 10 m resolution across the Canadian Prairies. It was generated from bistatic X-band SAR observations acquired by the TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X satellites and can support terrain, slope, drainage, hydrology, and soil-moisture analyses. The dataset represents surface elevation rather than bare-earth terrain, so vegetation, buildings, voids, and radar-processing artefacts may affect some values.

Field Details Dataset ID NDAC-DEM-PRAIRIES-F25T26 Category Topography & Terrain Owner ACI Primary Contact Thuan Ha Spatial resolution 10 m Data types Raster Formats tiff Status Raw Last updated 2025-06-21

docs.text:
Legal land in Saskatchewan, Manitoba, and Alberta generally follows the Dominion Land Survey system. Each township contains 36 sections of approximately 640 acres, and each section is divided into four quarter sections - NE, NW, SE, and SW - of about 160 acres (65 hectares). A legal land description such as NE-16-74-20-W4 identifies the quarter, section, township, range, and meridian. Quarter-section data were obtained from ISC Saskatchewan, DataMB, and the Government of Alberta/AltaLIS

Field Details Dataset ID NDAC-QSECTION-PRAIRIES-F26T26 Category Other Resources Owner ACI Primary Contact Thuan Ha Spatial resolution 10 m Data types Vector Formats shp Status Raw Last updated 2025-06-21

docs.title: 🗺️ Yield report
docs.text: Processed Internal

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A compiled spatial dataset of crop yield data for the Canadian Prairies, aggregated from publicly available provincial agricultural reporting portals. Data are organized by AFSC risk-map zones for Alberta and by Rural Municipality (RM) for Saskatchewan and Manitoba. File types include shapefiles (cpg, dbf, prj, shp, shx), raster imagery (tif), tabular data (csv), metadata (xml), and documentation (txt). Top-level folders are AB_Risk_Area, MB_Rural_Municipality, and SK_Rural_Municipality.

Field Details Dataset ID NDAC-YIELD-PRAIRIES-F1938-T2025 Category Thematic Map Products Owner ACI Primary Contact Thuan Ha Temporal coverage 2015 - 2025 Data types Raster Formats tiff Status Processed Last updated 2026-07-06

docs.title: 📍 Yield survey
docs.text: Processed Restricted

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The PPSN Yield Dataset is an internal, point-based agricultural yield-monitor dataset prepared by the Nutrien Digital Agriculture Centre (NDAC),. The yield dataset derived from priaries_wide_yield-data_cleaned and generated by the PPSN area-of-interest extraction pipeline. The dataset represents individual observations recorded by agricultural combines during harvest. Each point contains geographic coordinates, harvest date, crop and field identifiers, combine-operating measurements, raw yield, a filtered yield estimate, and several quality-control flags.

docs.title: 🌐 Saskatchewan Soil Infomation System
docs.text: Live Open

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Saskatchewan Soil Information System (SKSIS) is an interactive web-mapping platform for exploring Saskatchewan’s soil surveys and related environmental information. It provides soil classifications, landscape characteristics, agricultural capability, texture, salinity, and other properties for the province’s agricultural region. The survey maps are generally interpreted at approximately 1:100,000 scale and represent soil polygons rather than individual fields or quarter sections.

Field Details Dataset ID USASK-SOIL-SKSIS-WEBMAP Category External Map Portals
